newsitem.title: USA: Hedge funds do best in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Hedge funds do best in Russia.

text.p: Hedge funds specializing in emerging market equity investing were the top performers among hedge funds in the first quarter 1997, with the best returns coming from investments in Russia, fund peformance monitor TASS Management Ltd said.
Emerging market equity hedge funds posted average returns of 21.29 percent in the first quarter.
Emerging market equity funds ranked as the top hedge fund category for 1996 as well, with average returns of 36.59 pct.

"It was principally those funds which invested solely or primarily in the Russian equity markets that won emerging market funds top ratings for the quarter," TASS Management chief executive, Nicola Meaden, said.
"This Russian market clearly has demonstrated that it still has plenty of steam left in its bull run," she said.
The second best performing category for the first quarter was funds specializing in short selling of equities, which were up on average 18 percent.
Funds categorized as global macro hedge funds produced a return of 9.7 percent, while European equity funds were up 9.33 percent in the quarter.
Short sellers seemed to take advantage of the downward pressure and volatility in the U.S. equity markets in the first quarter, Meaden said.

Funds specializing in currency strategies and managed futures were the fifth and sixth best performing categories for the quarter, while U.S. equity funds posted the worst result of an average gain of 0.57 percent.
TASS Management Ltd is a London-based research company which tracks about 1,600 alternative investment managers and funds globally who manage about $9 billion in assets.
"Alternative" investments programs include hedge funds, Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs), managed currency programs, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
